quote: MSL agrees to protect, defend, hold harmless, and indemnify IBM from and against any and all claims, damages, liabilities, losses and expenses, arising out of the following, whether alleged or actual:
rationale: Section 15.1 gives us a full vendor-side defence and indemnity from MSL covering (a) third-party IP infringement (patent, trademark, copyright, mask work, trade secret) arising from MSL's performance or MSL-procured parts, designs, deliverables and pre-existing materials, (b) MSL's failure to comply with applicable law, and (c) MSL's failure to perform its warranty and support obligations — squarely the preferred position on IP, breach of law and MSL misconduct. The carve-outs are appropriately narrow and limited to claims caused by IBM-selected marks, IBM's written specifications or IBM-provided defective designs, i.e. our own inputs, rather than the broad "modification/combination" exclusions the fallback would tolerate. Section 15.2 contains only standard procedural conditions (prompt notice, cooperation, MSL control of defence with our right to participate at our own expense) and MSL's forward-looking cure options in 15.2(b) are at MSL's expense and do not displace its payment obligation or cap the indemnity. Appendix A item 5 adds a further MSL indemnity for Microsoft code matters in IBM's favour. There is no reciprocal IBM indemnity for MSL's services, so the direction of risk is correct. Minor points noted but not flagged: the indemnity does not expressly name a data-breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct prong, and 16.21 lets MSL suspend supply where a claim stems from IBM-specified designs — sub-elements short of preferred wording that do not affect the material terms.

rationale: Ownership runs in our favour and meets the preferred position. Section 13.1 (p0197) has MSL assign to IBM all IP rights in the hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered, and p0198 gives IBM ownership of MSL inventions on Products and on IBM processes/systems, with only a narrow carve-out letting MSL use such inventions in performing its obligations to us (an operational licence back to the vendor that does not prejudice us). Section 13.3(a) (p0208) confirms no rights or licences in IBM's pre-existing IP pass to MSL beyond a royalty-free right to use IBM confidential information solely to manufacture Products for IBM, with any further licence requiring a separate signed IBM agreement; §13.2 keeps IBM information under the AECI with a return-on-request right. Section 5 of the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement (p1530) keeps title to all Loaned Items with IBM. Nothing assigns IBM IP or IBM data to MSL, no vendor ownership of deliverables and no joint ownership appears (searches for "joint ownership" and "property of MSL" return nothing; p0947's "MSL will own the entire manufacturing and delivery process" is operational responsibility, not an IP grant). quote: Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, MSL agrees to produce and sell, and IBM agrees to purchase Products. This Agreement does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product.
rationale: The agreement contains no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on IBM, so it meets the preferred position. Purchasing is order-driven: Section 6.0 obliges IBM to purchase Products only "[s]ubject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement" with no requirements/volume commitment, and Section 6.1 lets IBM "cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time." Searches for "exclusive", "sole supplier", requirements-from and third-party-sourcing restrictions surfaced only (i) an entire-agreement clause, (ii) MSL's exclusive remedy in the loan agreement, and (iii) restrictions running against MSL (e.g. MSL may use IBM Parts and assets solely in IBM Products), none of which restrict IBM's freedom to source from other suppliers. The IBM responsibilities list (Section 4.0) and the Supply Flexibility provisions likewise impose no minimum-share or single-source commitment. No redline required.

quote: 13.1 IBM assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered under this Agreement
rationale: Every licence grant in this Agreement runs from us (IBM) to MSL, not to us: § 13.3(a) grants MSL only a royalty-free licence to use IBM confidential information necessary to manufacture Products solely for IBM (with any broader licence requiring a separate signed IBM agreement); the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement §§ 5 and 6 grant MSL a limited licence to use Loaned Programs and to execute Licensed Internal Code; and Appendix A expressly confirms MSL receives no rights in MS Software Images. Searches for any inbound grant ("grants IBM", "license to IBM", royalty-free, perpetual/irrevocable/sublicense) return no licence in our favour, and none is needed because § 13.1/13.2 give us outright ownership plus MSL's assignment of all IP in the Products and of inventions made on Products and IBM processes — a stronger position than the preferred licence terms. Accordingly, the customer-side concerns in this rule (affiliate/contractor coverage, revocability at the Vendor's discretion, successor transferability) are inapplicable, and the restrictive, IBM-favourable grants should not be broadened. Noted only for the record: the § 12.2 continued-licensing mechanic for Loaned Programs binds MSL and is at IBM's discretion, again in our favour.

quote: If MSL suffers a substantially adverse change in its business, related to a reduction in IBM's Products requirements, including reductions of Products requirements due to migration to a competitive supplier, for the [*] from the Effective Date of this Agreement, MSL may terminate such number of Transferred Employees as it deems necessary.
rationale: The agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction binding IBM, which meets the preferred position (no restriction on the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build). I checked the sections most likely to carry such a covenant: § 6.0 Purchase of Products (p0720) creates only a purchase obligation for ordered Products with no requirements/exclusivity commitment; § 14.18 "Restrictions and Limitations" (p0995) and § 16.15 "Prohibited Suppliers" (p0319) restrict MSL, not IBM; and searches for "compete/competing/competitive", "exclusive", "sole/second source" and "IBM shall not" returned no restrictive covenant against us. The tangential hits are neutral or favourable to IBM: § 9.0(e) (p0186) expressly contemplates IBM reducing its Product requirements by migrating to a competitive supplier — confirming our freedom to dual-source; § 5.1(v) (p0116) is a mutual termination right on a change of control by a direct competitor; and the confidentiality agreement (p1491) preserves each party's freedom to provide competitive products and to supply the other's competitors. No redline is required.

quote: IBM may perform process audits at MSL's or an MSL Related Company's Work Center or MSL's subcontractors' facilities to assure that identified IBM specifications have been complied with.
rationale: The rule targets audit/verification rights binding us as customer, and none exist in this agreement. Every audit and inspection right runs in our favour against MSL: §7.0 (IBM process audits at MSL Work Centers, with advance notice to MSL), §13.1 (IBM audit/inspection of consigned Products), §21.3 and §21.2 (IBM inspection of IBM-owned tooling), §24.1 (IBM retains the right to audit software use), Attachment 6 §4.0 (IBM monitoring/inspection/audit of MSL software installation locations, limited to MSL's business hours per p1314), and Attachment 6 Appendix A §4 (IBM/MS audit of MSL's books and records on 45 days' notice by an independent CPA, at IBM's cost unless material discrepancies, and no more frequently than semiannually). MSL is given no reciprocal right to audit or inspect IBM's books, records, facilities or systems, and there is no remote-access-to-our-systems language anywhere. §16.14 imposes only a mutual five-year record-retention obligation related to the manufacture of Products; it creates no verification or access right for MSL, so the residual burden on us is a modest recordkeeping duty rather than an audit right. Because nothing binds us, the preferred position's frequency, notice, cost and no-system-access limits are unnecessary, and no redline is warranted. Note for the file: should MSL later seek a reciprocal audit right (for example over IBM-supplied volume, consumption or pricing data), we should hold it to once per 12 months on 30 days' written notice, off-site review by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at MSL's cost unless an underpayment above 5% is found, with no direct access to our systems.

rationale: The only most-favoured-nation language in the Agreement runs in our favour: MSL undertakes that its engineering will be priced to IBM on a "most favored customer" basis (p1099), i.e. the Vendor grants the Customer best pricing. Searches for reciprocal formulations ("less favorable", "best price", third-party matching) and review of the pricing provisions (§ 7.0, § 8.2 Parts Cost Reductions) found no obligation requiring IBM to extend MSL terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers; the tooling right of first refusal at p1104 is an IBM option, not an MFN burden. Section 5.2 a) iii (p0130) requires MSL, within a stated number of days after expiration or termination, to return to IBM all copies of IBM Product documentation and all confidential documents, discs, tapes and other media containing IBM confidential information, satisfying the data-return limb; Section 13.2 c) (p0204) additionally lets IBM demand immediate return of all confidential information at any time during the term. Attachment 6 §3(a) (p1435) adds return plus signed written certification for MS Software Image media and documentation. quote: a) MSL expressly warrants that all Products, MSL supplied materials and Parts, and work prepared for IBM will conform in all material respects to the specifications, drawings, or other descriptions furnished or adopted by IBM, and will be of specified quality, good workmanship, and free from defect subject to the following terms:
rationale: SOW Section 19 contains a genuine express performance warranty running in our favour: MSL warrants that all Products, supplied materials/Parts and work conform in all material respects to IBM-furnished specifications and are of specified quality, good workmanship and free from defect (p1059), with stated warranty periods for MSL Procured Parts (p1063) and workmanship (p1067) measured in months (figures redacted as [*]), commencing on delivery to IBM, surviving acceptance testing and expressly covering latent defects (p1068). The remedy set is at or above the preferred position: Failure Analysis, repair or replacement within a set turnaround, and a refund of MSL's price (plus Parts prices) where repair or replacement is not possible (p1077), supplemented by MSL bearing Product Recall costs on epidemic failure (p1086) and a clean-title warranty (p1075). The Section 19.6 "in lieu of" language (p1079/p1083) disclaims only implied/other terms and is expressly framed as replacing them with "MSL'S WARRANTY OBLIGATIONS DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION 19" — it does not swallow the express warranty, so this is nowhere near the "AS IS" walk-away. Minor sub-elements short of the model wording are noted only: there is no express "no malicious code" warranty and no standalone conformance-to-documentation software warranty (compliance with law is handled separately at Section 16.4), and the warranty durations are redacted; these are not material failures of the fallback and we do not redline them.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a standard insurance covenant: the Agreement has no programme-level coverage requirement even though MSL holds IBM inventory and tooling, works with IBM premises and accesses IBM systems and data. Limits are our standard position (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where MSL processes IBM or IBM customer data); we can work with E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M if needed.

ops.text:
16.22 Insurance

MSL shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law; and, where MSL processes IBM or IBM customer data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. MSL shall provide certificates of insurance to IBM upon request. This Section is in addition to, and does not limit, any insurance obligation of MSL elsewhere in this Agreement or its Attachments.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 16.22 (Insurance) requiring MSL to carry CGL, E&O, workers' compensation and cyber coverage and provide certificates.

quote: MSL will provide replacement value insurance coverage for consigned Products. IBM will be named as a joint insured with respect to consigned Products for its interest.
rationale: The Agreement contains no programme-level vendor insurance covenant. The only insurance references are asset-specific or cost allocations: p0909 (replacement-value cover on consigned Products with IBM as joint insured), p1107 (IBM insures its own tooling, MSL jointly insured where possible) and p0649/p0863 (freight insurance as a price component). None requires MSL to carry commercial general liability, professional liability/E&O, workers' compensation or cyber/data coverage, so the clause falls short of even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). MSL is an outsourced manufacturer that holds IBM inventory and tooling, operates from leased IBM premises and accesses IBM applications, networks and customer data (§ 24.1), so the rule applies and the omission is material. We propose inserting a short Section 16.22 in the General article at the preferred limits, noting the fallback in the comment.

verification.notes: All five preferred coverage lines (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M conditioned on data processing, workers' comp, certificates on request) appear expressly in the inserted Section 16.22, so the locked preferred level is complete. The insertion is a concise stand-alone covenant for a clause that was wholly absent from the Agreement, which is the minimal available means; no existing sentence was rewritten or deleted. The 'for one (1) year thereafter' tail and the non-limitation sentence go marginally beyond the stated position, but the tail is a short customer-favourable add-on and the non-limitation sentence prevents conflict with the existing consigned-Products and tooling insurance obligations, so neither is a material over-reach. No undefined terms, contradictions or dangling mechanics introduced; the surrounding consigned-inventory and tooling provisions remain fully effective.

quote: This Agreement will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Both term clauses auto-renew with non-renewal notice windows far beyond the fallback ceiling of 60 days: Base Agreement § 4.0 requires six months (approx. 180 days) notice, and the Attachment § 2.0 requires twelve months' notice to escape a further six-month renewal. Windows longer than 90 days are walk-away territory, so this fails the fallback on a material term. The redline takes the clause to the preferred position: IBM may opt out on 30 days' notice, renewals are 12 months, MSL must send a reminder 60 days before renewal, and any renewal price increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. MSL's own notice period is left untouched to protect supply continuity.

verification.notes: All four preferred atomic elements are present in operative text: 12-month automatic renewal terms, a 30-day Customer (IBM) opt-out, a mandatory 60-day MSL reminder, and a renewal price cap at the lesser of CPI and 3%. Edits are surgical: two targeted replacements of the notice/renewal-period language and one concise inserted sentence supplying the absent reminder and price-cap mechanics; MSL's own notice period and the unchanged sentences (term length, successive-periods language, Section 5.0 termination rights) remain effective. Changing the Attachment's renewal period from six (6) to twelve (12) months is required by the preferred position's 12-month renewal cycle, so it is not an extraneous change. Minor, rationale-only notes: 'CPI' is used without a defined index/measurement period, and the reminder/price-cap sentence is inserted only after the Base Agreement term paragraph, so its application to the Attachment renewals depends on incorporation by reference rather than express repetition.

mappings.element: Customer termination for convenience.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a convenience exit for IBM as Customer on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, because Section 5.0 permits termination only for cause during a three-year committed term, and confirmed MSL has no matching convenience right.

ops.text: 5.4 Termination for Convenience. Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon 30 days' prior written notice to MSL, and MSL shall refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any fees prepaid for the period after the effective date of termination. MSL shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial term or any renewal term.

proposal.summary: Add Section 5.4 giving Customer (IBM) a 30-day convenience termination right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; MSL has no convenience right during a term.

quote: This Agreement shall become effective on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of three (3) years unless terminated as provided in Section 5.0. This Agreement will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: The Agreement runs for a committed three-year initial term (p0104) and Section 5.1 permits termination only "for cause" — uncured material breach, insolvency, acquisition by a competitor, or continuing force majeure (p0107, p0110, p0116). There is no convenience exit for us during the term; the six-month notice in Section 4.0 is only a non-renewal right at term end, and the Purchase Order cancellation right is order-level and subject to cancellation charges. That is walk-away territory under T4C, so we insert a new Section 5.4 giving Customer a 30 days' notice convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and confirming MSL has no convenience right during the initial or any renewal term (preferred position).

verification.notes: All four atomic elements of the preferred position are expressly present in the inserted Section 5.4: Customer convenience right, 30 days' prior written notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and an express bar on Vendor (MSL) convenience termination during the initial or any renewal term. Locked target level is achieved. The fallback is not satisfied (30 days rather than 60–90 days, no early-termination fee, no end-of-term Vendor right), but that is immaterial because the preferred bargain is fully met and the terms are more favourable to us. Minimality holds: a single concise inserted clause fills a genuine gap (Section 5.0 otherwise permits termination only for cause during the three-year committed term); no untouched sentence was rewritten and no new exception was created. Intent concern: the insertion uses "Customer", which is not a defined term in this Agreement — the parties are defined as "IBM" and "MSL". As drafted the right and the refund obligation run to an undefined party, creating a dangling mechanic. Replace "Customer" with "IBM" throughout the inserted clause.
